reviewed_primary_facts.fact: Every scroll property node is marked for snapping before composited versus non-composited scrolling is distinguished.

Scroll snapping rounds screen translation, then maps the correction back through the inverse screen transform. Potential animation, non-axis-aligned transforms and noninvertible ancestry disable this operation.
Screen translation uses std::round, including half values of negative translations.

Scroll-contents promotion is independent of the snapping decision; LCD preference can retain non-composited scrolling when the first scrolling paint chunk does not cover the entire contents with opacity.
Client geometry starts inside borders and scrollbar insets, while in-flow padding contributes to reachable content bounds.

Stable gutters reserve the writing-mode inline axis for hidden, auto and scroll overflow, excluding overlay scrollbars and the viewport-defining element. Both-edges mirrors the reserved gutter. The left scrollbar is clamped to the content width.
